headline: X and music publishers settle lawsuits after three-year legal battle
summary: The three-year legal dispute between X and major music publishers has concluded, with both sides opting to dismiss their opposing lawsuits. The terms of the settlement were not disclosed.
details: A protracted legal battle spanning three years between X (formerly Twitter) and a consortium of major music publishers has quietly reached its conclusion. Court documents reveal that both parties have agreed to dismiss their respective lawsuits, though the specific terms of the settlement remain confidential.

The initial legal action was initiated by music publishers, who accused X of widespread copyright infringement, alleging that the platform profited from unlicensed music shared by its users. This led to a significant dispute over intellectual property rights on the social media platform.

Nearly three years later, X responded with its own countersuit, asserting that the music publishers were engaging in anticompetitive practices. X claimed these actions were designed to force the platform into licensing agreements at inflated rates, and recently argued it shouldn't be held responsible for user piracy.

Neither X nor the music publishers have offered public explanations for the dismissals. However, the court documents indicate that both suits were dismissed "with prejudice," meaning they are permanently closed and cannot be refiled in the future.

headline_marked: [[Google open-sources its 3D emoji]] set, making raw .OBJ files available for creators
headline: Google open-sources its 3D emoji set, making raw .OBJ files available for creators
summary: Google's Noto Emoji 3D, which debuted in May, can now be used by developers and creators to build immersive VR worlds, indie apps, or unique memes.
details: Google has officially open-sourced its entire Noto Emoji 3D set, providing raw .OBJ files to the community. This move allows developers and creators to integrate Google's distinctive 3D emoji into their own projects.

The open-sourcing enables a wide range of applications, from building immersive virtual reality environments to developing indie apps or creating new memes. This initiative was announced as part of World Emoji Day, offering new creative possibilities.

Google also shared insights into the design process behind its 3D pictograms, highlighting the complexities of translating 2D concepts into three dimensions. Questions like whether a smiley face is a sphere or a flat disc become crucial in 3D modeling.
caption:
Google just open-sourced its entire 3D emoji collection!

Google has officially open-sourced its entire Noto Emoji 3D set, providing raw .OBJ files to the community. This move allows developers and creators to integrate Google's distinctive 3D emoji into their own projects.

The open-sourcing enables a wide range of applications, from building immersive virtual reality environments to developing indie apps or creating new memes. This initiative was announced as part of World Emoji Day, offering new creative possibilities.

Google also shared insights into the design process behind its 3D pictograms, highlighting the complexities of translating 2D concepts into three dimensions. Questions like whether a smiley face is a sphere or a flat disc become crucial in 3D modeling.
